text:
Evan: hi folks, new hire here. grabbed a hosted API key from the Console for a quick demo but after a few streaming requests I get 429s and the socket closes. Is that just expected on a dev laptop? :thinking_face:
Sam (DevEx): welcome Evan! hosted keys are fine for demos but they're in tighter rate buckets and can be subject to IP allowlists. For interactive dev use the sandbox key or a CI token. Sandbox supports streaming but with smaller burst quotas.
Evan: ok makes sense. my app reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env. quickest way to switch to sandbox for testing?
Sam (DevEx): simplest: export a sandbox token locally. Example for a quick curl streaming test:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-sandbox-xxxxx"
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-mini-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Nina: note: if you're on corp VPN or using a proxy the hosted key may hit org-level egress IPs that are rate-limited or not allowlisted; that can make chunked streams fail. Sandbox tokens usually bypass those allowlists.
Evan: my local test still hit a burst limit on sandbox after ~10 short streams. how do I request more for a demo window?
Sam (DevEx): file a temporary quota request: https://redwood.internal/devex/keys-requests. Include team, repo, expected qps, and time window. We can grant short-lived increases for scheduled demos. Or email devex@redwood.ai.
Evan: storing the sandbox token in a .env on my laptop ok?
Sam (DevEx): fine for personal dev but never commit. Add .env to .gitignore. Prefer OS keyring or the local secret store when possible. For CI use the Console -> Service tokens -> CI token flow so you don't put hosted keys in CI.
Nina: another trick: reduce batch_size and max_tokens for dev, and enable SDK debug to see retries/backoff behavior. That cuts quota burn and surfaces whether the 429s are client-side batching spikes.
Evan: any ops fix if the hosted key is needed for a live customer demo?
Sam (DevEx): if hosted access is required, open a ticket for IP allowlist with infra and include your devbox IP. Also schedule a temporary sandbox quota bump if you want to run more parallel streams.
infra-bot: Tip: Exponential backoff + jitter on 429s is recommended. If you see persistent 429s include the short request id and timestamp and we can inspect the bucket.
Evan: sweet, swapping to sandbox now. thanks!
onboarding-bot: Welcome to Redwood! See onboarding checklist: https://redwood.internal/onboarding and ping @Sam (DevEx) if you need help with keys.
